name: Petty Cash Manager
summary: Petty cash app for small businesses: cash floats per custodian, receipt scanning, staff submissions with approval, automatic VAT or GST split and export files for Zoho Books, QuickBooks and Xero. Works offline in the browser.
best_for: small businesses that run an imprest petty cash float (shops, restaurants, site offices, clinics, schools) and want receipts, approvals and the VAT split in one simple app
skip_if: you need full expense management with corporate cards and reimbursements, or your accounting software already handles petty cash well enough
honest_knock: Without the Cloud sync add-on, your records live in the browser on each device: lose the phone without a recent backup and the data is gone, and a team cannot share one ledger. The licence is checked online about once a week. After the trial, existing entries stay viewable but adding new ones needs a paid licence. It is a small, single-purpose tool from a small vendor; check that it does what your accountant needs before moving your petty cash process onto it.

pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-02 on pettycash.getdailytools.com, pricing section and FAQ; the page says prices are in US dollars, with VAT or GST added at checkout where your country requires it) Petty Cash Manager has one app and four ways to pay, and every plan includes every feature. The difference is the billing term and the number of devices: Monthly is $7 a month on 2 devices; 3 months is $16.99 ($5.66 a month) on 3 devices; 6 months is $26.99 ($4.50 a month) on 5 devices; Yearly is $41.99 ($3.50 a month) on 6 devices. Cloud sync, which keeps a shared copy on the vendor's EU cloud server so a team sees the same entries, is an add-on of +$3 a month on any plan. Plans renew automatically and can be cancelled any time; there is a 14-day free trial without a card and a full refund if you email within 14 days of any payment. The page also shows a launch offer: 50% off your first payment for the first 20 customers, until 18 November 2026. Re-read on 14 November 2026 with a plain fetch of pettycash.getdailytools.com: Monthly $7 (2 devices), 3 months $16.99 (3 devices), 6 months $26.99 (5 devices), Yearly $41.99 (6 devices), Cloud sync +$3 a month, unchanged. The advertised savings check out against $7 a month: $5.66 is 19% less, $4.50 is 36% less and $3.50 is 50% less. The launch offer (50% off the first payment for the first 20 customers) still runs until 18 November 2026.

schema_offer.description: Monthly, billed monthly, 2 devices; 3 months $16.99 (3 devices), 6 months $26.99 (5 devices), yearly $41.99 (6 devices, $3.50 a month); every plan has every feature; Cloud sync is +$3 a month on any plan; VAT or GST added at checkout where required. Read on the vendor's own pricing page on 2026-11-14.

compare_with.name: Shoeboxed
compare_with.why: both turn receipts into bookkeeping data. Shoeboxed is a receipt-scanning service with mail-in paper digitization and plans billed per scan volume; Petty Cash Manager is narrower: it tracks cash floats per custodian, approvals and the tax split, and exports to Zoho Books, QuickBooks or Xero

claims.claim: Try free for 14 days first, no card
claims.observed: The app opened with Free trial: 14 days left and no card, account or e-mail address was asked; the setup form and sample data came straight after.
claims.plan: 14 day free trial in the browser; the Yearly + Cloud checkout was viewed, nothing was paid
claims.comparability: The line on the plan page against the trial banner and a start without any sign-in.
claims.buying_consequence: You can try the app for 14 days without giving any payment or personal details.

claims.claim: Teams where several cashiers record spending
claims.observed: The dossier group of teams with several cashiers depends on Cloud sync. The staff link per custodian was not used and Cloud sync was not switched on, so recording by several people was not tested.
claims.plan: 14 day free trial in the browser; the Yearly + Cloud checkout was viewed, nothing was paid
claims.comparability: The dossier group against a test with one local browser and one custodian.
claims.buying_consequence: Whether several cashiers can work in one shared set of entries is not confirmed by this test.

claims.claim: The photo stays on your device.
claims.observed: The app shows this line when a receipt photo is added and says data stays on the device until Cloud sync is on. Network traffic was not inspected, so it is the claim of the app that was not checked.
claims.plan: 14 day free trial in the browser; the Yearly + Cloud checkout was viewed, nothing was paid
claims.comparability: The message in the app against a test without network inspection.
claims.buying_consequence: The vendor says the receipt photo stays on your device; this was not checked at the network level.

claims.observed: The first expense of 4.50 with a receipt photo was saved after about 6 steps and the balance showed 495.50 with 4.50 under Awaiting approval, from a float of 500.
claims.plan: 14 day free trial in the browser; the Yearly + Cloud checkout was viewed, nothing was paid
claims.comparability: Our own count of the steps and amounts for one expense; later expenses were added by a script on the form fields.
claims.buying_consequence: Recording one expense with a photo is quick, and the balance follows the float at once.

claims.claim: No e-invoice QR code found on this photo.
claims.observed: The app looked for an e-invoice QR code on the made up receipt and found none, and offered Read the total from the photo, which was not used.
claims.plan: 14 day free trial in the browser; the Yearly + Cloud checkout was viewed, nothing was paid
claims.comparability: The message in the app against a photo without a QR code; the read-the-total button was not tried.
claims.buying_consequence: Whether the app reads the total from a real receipt photo is not confirmed; our test receipt had no QR code.

claims.plan: 14 day free trial in the browser; the Yearly + Cloud checkout was viewed, nothing was paid
claims.comparability: Our own sum of the 8 approved amounts against the report; the 144.54 total of all 10 was not shown by the report.

claims.observed: The Entries export gave petty-cash-all.csv of 1259 bytes with 11 lines: a header and the 10 expenses, with columns for date, ref, custodian, category, net, tax, total and status. The file was not opened further.
claims.plan: 14 day free trial in the browser; the Yearly + Cloud checkout was viewed, nothing was paid
claims.comparability: The line count of the downloaded file against 10 expenses; no cell values were compared.
claims.buying_consequence: You can get the entries out as a CSV file for a spreadsheet; the cell contents were not checked.

claims.observed: The report has Print and PDF buttons. They were not used, because the print and PDF dialog was avoided, so the PDF report was not seen.
claims.plan: 14 day free trial in the browser; the Yearly + Cloud checkout was viewed, nothing was paid

claims.observed: The report offers exports for Zoho Books, QuickBooks and Xero. None was used, so the files and their import were not seen.
claims.plan: 14 day free trial in the browser; the Yearly + Cloud checkout was viewed, nothing was paid

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session tested Petty Cash Manager on its 14 day free trial in the browser: after about 6 steps the first expense with a receipt photo was saved, and 10 test expenses later 8 were approved and 1 rejected, and the november report showed 127.24 for 8 entries, split by category. The CSV export had a header and 10 lines. Everything stays on the device: no account, no cloud, and a banner asks you to download a backup. Cloud sync, which needs an e-mail code, was not tested. The page says Cloud sync costs +$3 a month on any plan, but that is true only for the Monthly plan: Yearly goes from $41.99 to $69.99, which is +$28 a year. Cancelling is only possible after paying. Nothing was paid. Account and start: the app is local in the browser and has no separate account; our Chrome, who created the account, was signed in, and our AI assistant ran the test in its own tab, starting at about 13:54 on the clock of the shell, which ran unreliably fast, so no durations are taken from it. The interface was already in English and the free trial said Free trial: 14 days left. The dossier name is Petty Cash Manager and the review is on OSM (petty-cash-manager-review). Start: the first screen was the setup form Set up your petty cash (Country Other, Currency USD, Tax 0, Language English, the box for anonymous usage counts left unticked). The app then showed sample data, which was cleared with Clear sample data and start. Core action: a custodian Test Cashier (Test Shop, float 500, opening cash 500) and then a first expense of 4.50, category Office supplies, paid to Sample Shop, description Test pens, with a receipt photo of a made up receipt. It saved with Saved, the balance became 495.50 and Awaiting approval 4.50. That took about 6 steps: 1 setup form, 1 clearing the sample data, 1 custodian with 4 fields, 1 expense with 5 fields and a photo, and Save. The receipt photo: the app said Looking for the e-invoice QR code..., then No e-invoice QR code found on this photo, with a button Read the total from the photo (not used), and says The photo stays on your device. Nine more expenses were added (3.20 Courier & postage, 12.80 Coffee, 25.00 Miscellaneous cleaning, 9.99 Office, 6.40 Transport, 18.75 Tools, 7.30 Meals, 41.00 Utilities, 15.60 coffee beans), 10 entries and 144.54 USD in total; the form fields were filled by a script on the real fields and Save was clicked on the button. Approvals: 8 were approved, 1 was rejected and 1 stayed waiting. The report for november 2026 shows APPROVED EXPENSES 127.24 (8 entries), NET 127.24 USD, RECOVERABLE INPUT TAX 0.00, CASH ADDED 500.00 and the spending by category (Utilities 41.00, Miscellaneous 25.00, Meals & refreshments 22.90, Tools & hardware 18.75, Office supplies 9.99, Transport 6.40, Courier & postage 3.20); the categories add up to 127.24. The report offers Print, PDF, Export to Excel (CSV) for the Input Tax register and exports for Zoho Books, QuickBooks and Xero. Export: Entries, Export to Excel (CSV) gave petty-cash-all.csv (1259 bytes, 11 lines: a header and 10 expenses, columns Date, Ref, Type, Custodian, Category, Paid to, Invoice no., Description, Cash source, Net, Tax, Total, Status, Note; refs Nov00126 to Nov01026). The file was not opened further and the PDF report was not opened (the print and PDF dialog was avoided). Local or cloud: everything is stored locally in the browser. Settings, Backup & restore says Your data stays on this device. Download a backup regularly and keep it safe, and Browser storage: Not protected, the browser may clear it if space runs low; a banner says no backup was downloaded yet and that the data is gone if the browser is cleared. Cloud sync is included in the free trial and after the trial needs a + Cloud plan; signing in needs an e-mail address and a sign-in code, which was NOT tested (no e-mail or code was used). When cloud sync is on, entries and receipt photos are also stored on the cloud server of the vendor. The staff link per custodian was not used. Plans: The plans were read by the tester on 18 Nov 2026 on the vendor site (pettycash.getdailytools.com, section pricing) and read again just before this delivery the same day, with the same prices. On this device: Monthly $7 a month on 2 devices, 3 months $16.99 ($5.66 a month, Save 19%) on 3 devices, 6 months $26.99 ($4.50 a month, Save 36%) on 5 devices, Yearly $41.99 ($3.50 a month, Save 50%) on 6 devices. With Cloud sync: Monthly $10 a month on 2 devices, 3 months $24.99 ($8.33 a month), 6 months $41.99 ($7 a month), Yearly $69.99 ($5.83 a month), on 2, 3, 5 and 6 devices. Prices are in US dollars; VAT or GST is added at checkout where your country requires it. The page says Try free for 14 days first, no card, a 14-day money-back guarantee and Renews automatically, cancel any time. The prices on the live vendor page are unchanged and match the dossier. Difference on the page: the page and the FAQ say Add Cloud sync to any plan for +$3 a month. In the prices Cloud sync costs +$3 a month only on the Monthly plan; Yearly goes from $41.99 to $69.99 (+$28 a year, $2.33 a month), 6 months from $26.99 to $41.99 (+$15, $2.50 a month) and 3 months from $16.99 to $24.99 (+$8.01, $2.67 a month). Checkout: the vendor site opened a Lemon Squeezy checkout for Petty Cash Manager (Yearly + Cloud) with US$ 69,99 billed every 12 months, Subtotaal US$ 69,99, Totaal US$ 69,99 and the button US$ 69,99 betalen; no tax was shown yet because no address was entered. The payment methods were card, PayPal and Link, Google Pay and Cash App Pay. Nothing was filled in or clicked except opening the page; the checkout showed saved payment details of the account owner, so no screenshot of it was kept, and the checkout was left. The cookie banner of the vendor site was set to Decline. Cancelling: there is no cancel button in the app and no account, since the trial is local. The FAQ says you cancel at any time from the link in your receipt e-mail, with the plan staying active until the end of the paid period, and that an e-mail within 14 days of a payment gives a full refund. So cancelling is only possible after paying. Settings has Erase all data at the bottom (local, not clicked); deleting a cloud account was not seen. Not tested: cloud sync (needs an e-mail code), the staff link, reading the total from the photo, the PDF report, the Zoho Books, QuickBooks and Xero exports, the language switch, installing as an app, and paying. Clean up: the test data stays in the browser storage of our Chrome: the custodian Test Cashier, 10 test expenses and 1 receipt photo; the sample data was cleared; the file petty-cash-all.csv is still in the Downloads folder; our own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: Your data lives in the browser only, which the app itself calls not protected, so you have to download a backup yourself or it can be gone when the browser is cleared. Teams that want several devices to share entries need Cloud sync, which we could not try, and which costs less than +$3 a month on the longer plans but more than the plan price alone. There is no cancel button in the app: you cancel from the link in your receipt e-mail after you have paid. The receipt photo scan found no e-invoice QR code on our test receipt, so the total had to be typed in.

friction.export_route: The CSV export petty-cash-all.csv was downloaded (1259 bytes, a header and 10 expenses) but not opened further; no kit records were entered and no reimport was run.

not_tested: Cloud sync, which needs an e-mail sign-in code.
The staff link, reading the total from the receipt photo and the PDF report.
The Zoho Books, QuickBooks and Xero exports, the language switch and installing as an app.
Paying, and cancelling, which is only possible from the receipt e-mail after payment.
Tax on the checkout, which showed no amount before an address was entered.
Export of a file into a kit, and reimport.
